title: A localization of a regular ring is regular
statement: Let $R$ be a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] (Noetherian, with every localization at a prime ideal a regular local ring), let $M\subseteq R$ be a multiplicative subset ($1\in M$, $st\in M$ for $s,t\in M$), and let $\varphi:R\to R'$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings which is a localization of $R$ at $M$: (a) $\varphi(s)$ is a unit for every $s\in M$; (b) every element of $R'$ is $\varphi(r)\varphi(s)^{-1}$ with $r\in R$, $s\in M$; (c) $\varphi(r)=0$ implies $sr=0$ for some $s\in M$ (for instance $R'=M^{-1}R$). Then $R'$ is a regular ring.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0381 (lemma-geometrically-regular, line 47104), Step 3: 'a localization of a regular ring (immediate from the definition)'; Definition Tag 00OD (regular ring); Noetherianity: Lemma Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence); primes of a localization: Lemma Tag 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization)

proof.text: $R'$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The regular ring $R$ is Noetherian by definition [def-weil-regular-scheme], and $\varphi$ satisfies (a), (b), (c) for $M$, which are exactly the hypotheses (a), (b), (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] with $S=M$ (that node is stated for any localization in this sense, not only for $M^{-1}R$). Hence $R'$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence, line 5991): any localization of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q'\subset R'$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak q=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q')$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] with $A=R$, $W=M$, $\lambda=\varphi$, $A'=R'$ (its hypotheses are (a), (b), (c) verbatim): by its part (1), $\mathfrak q$ is a prime ideal of $R$ with $\mathfrak q\cap M=\emptyset$; by its part (2), the map $\theta:R_{\mathfrak q}\to R'_{\mathfrak q'}$, $a/s\mapsto\varphi(a)/\varphi(s)$, between the localizations at primes [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras, in particular a ring isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization, line 3163) for the primes of a localization; basic notion Tag 00C9 (item-localization-localization, line 223) for the localization of a localization

proof.text: $R'_{\mathfrak q'}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Since $R$ is regular and $\mathfrak q$ is a prime of $R$ (Step 2), $R_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring: Noetherian, local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak qR_{\mathfrak q}$, and $\mathfrak m$ generated by $d=\dim R_{\mathfrak q}$ elements $x_1,\dots,x_d$. The ring isomorphism $\theta$ of Step 2 maps ideals bijectively to ideals, preserving inclusions and primality, so $R'_{\mathfrak q'}$ is Noetherian, local with maximal ideal $\theta(\mathfrak m)$ (the unique maximal ideal is carried to the unique maximal ideal), of Krull dimension $d$ (chains of primes correspond), and $\theta(\mathfrak m)$ is generated by $\theta(x_1),\dots,\theta(x_d)$. Hence $R'_{\mathfrak q'}$ is a regular local ring. (In Mathlib this transport is IsRegularLocalRing.of_ringEquiv, Mathlib/RingTheory/RegularLocalRing/Defs.lean line 68.)
